conclusion: Plain SetCountLimit(1) consumes its per-instance local count at activation and this limit is not automatically refunded by activation negation. OATH auxiliary restrictions and explicit COUNT_CODE_OATH counters have separate removal/refund paths.

citations.meaning: SetCountLimit default code=0 and flag=0; no implicit OATH flag.
dec_count decrements local count_limit for code=flag=0.
Activation negation removes oath effects and decrements the shared effect-code count only when COUNT_CODE_OATH is set.
inc_count is exposed only as explicit RestoreCountLimit Lua API in this complete core.
All 22953 pinned Lua scripts searched; RestoreCountLimit occurs only 3 times in proc_xyz.lua, not global negation handling.

limitations: Technical secondary implementation references, not newly authenticated Konami rulings.
The distinction between count limits and an OATH cannot-attack restriction is intentional; removing the latter does not refund the paid detach or local effect count.
